finding.claim: ContentTypeParser.remove deletes the parser but never invalidates the lookup cache, so getParser keeps returning the removed parser from cache on subsequent requests.
finding.title: ContentTypeParser.remove does not clear cache

verifier.reason: Confirmed: getParser returns this.cache entries before consulting customParsers at content-type-parser.js:119-132, while remove at content-type-parser.js:170-190 only deletes from customParsers and splices parserList/parserRegExpList without clearing this.cache, unlike removeAll which resets the cache at content-type-parser.js:163-168.

finding.claim: arrange404 re-binds an already-bound defaultRoute, so the second prefixed instance has no effect and 404 fallback keeps the first instance as `this`.
finding.title: 404 defaultRoute double-bind loses instance

verifier.reason: The router is created with the unbound fourOhFourFallBack at four-oh-four.js:36, arrange404 unconditionally replaces router.defaultRoute with router.defaultRoute.bind(instance) at four-oh-four.js:49, and fourOhFourFallBack dereferences this[kFourOhFourLevelInstance] at four-oh-four.js:165; under Function.prototype.bind semantics a second bind cannot change the first bound this.

finding.claim: Socket timeout state stored on the reused keep-alive socket is overwritten per request and its cleanup only runs inside setupResponseListeners, which is skipped unless logger/onResponse/handlerTimeout is set, leaving stale request/reply and listener.
finding.title: Socket onTimeout handle replaced without guaranteed cleanup

verifier.reason: Route.js:559-561 gates setupResponseListeners on hasLogger/onResponse/handlerTimeout while route.js:563-568 unconditionally overwrites socket._meta for onTimeout, and the cited cleanup at reply.js:997-1001 is the normal-path removal, so a logger-disabled onTimeout route retains stale request/reply and the timeout listener; the hijack cleanup at reply.js:148-152 only covers hijacked replies, not normal completion.
